abstract: Grover’s quantum search and its generalization, quantum amplitude amplification, provide quadratic advantage over classical algorithms for a diverse set of tasks, but are tricky to use without knowing beforehand what fraction $\lambda$ of the initial state is comprised of the target states. In contrast, fixed-point search algorithms need only a reliable lower bound on this fraction, but, as a consequence, lose the very quadratic advantage that makes Grover’s algorithm so appealing. Here we provide the first version of amplitude amplification that achieves fixed-point behavior without sacrificing the quantum speedup. Our result incorporates an adjustable bound on the failure probability, and, for a given number of oracle queries, guarantees that this bound is satisfied over the broadest possible range of $\lambda$.

specification.problem: Construct a fixed-point version of quantum amplitude amplification that needs only a lower bound on the target fraction lambda of the initial state, retains the quadratic (Grover-type) query speedup, and guarantees an adjustable failure-probability bound over the broadest possible range of lambda for a given number of oracle queries.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Abstract-level problem statement plus minimal background equations for standard amplitude amplification and a failure-probability criterion. The specific fixed-point construction (phases, query count) is not given in the abstract and is not reconstructed.

equations.label: Initial target fraction
equations.description: Target fraction of the initial state under target projector Pi.
equations.abstract_quote: what fraction $\lambda$ of the initial state is comprised of the target states
equations.justification: Defines lambda as the target-state weight in the initial state.
assumptions: Pi is a projector onto target states

equations.label: Standard Grover success probability
equations.description: Success probability after k standard amplification iterations; requires knowing lambda to choose k.
equations.justification: Textbook amplitude amplification; shown for contrast, not as the paper's fixed-point method.

equations.label: Fixed-point failure guarantee
equations.description: Target guarantee: failure probability at most delta over a range of lambda with Q queries.
equations.abstract_quote: Our result incorporates an adjustable bound on the failure probability
equations.justification: Formalizes the adjustable failure bound; the range optimality is not derived.

registers.name: work
registers.role: holds the search state; initial state prepared by unitary A

registers.name: anc
registers.role: oracle flag qubit marking target states (assumed; could be absorbed in work)

steps.description: Prepare |psi_0> by applying the state-preparation unitary A to |0>.

Apply a sequence of Q oracle queries interleaved with reflections about |psi_0> using phases (generalized, non-Grover phases) chosen from delta and lambda_0 so that failure <= delta for all lambda >= lambda_0. The phase sequence is NOT given in the abstract and is left unspecified.
For contrast, standard amplification with k iterations needs lambda known to pick k, and overshoots otherwise.

specification.measurement: Measure the work register (with the flag qubit) in the computational basis after the Q queries; success means the outcome lies in the target subspace (projector Pi), which occurs with probability at least 1-delta for lambda >= lambda_0 (assumed from eq_3).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Check the measured outcome with the marking predicate (one classical or oracle check); accept if marked, otherwise repeat the run. Repetition count is not specified in the abstract.
